correctness.rationale: PASS. The three families of d² Fermat lines and the exact three cross-incidence congruences give a simple 3d²-vertex (4d-2)-regular graph with zero diagonal. Fourier basis indexed by (r,s) in (Z/d)^2 diagonalizes the within-family rook graph; cross-incidence couples only characters on the two diagonals. Nonconstant generic parameters form three Hermitian 2x2 blocks with eigenvalues d-2 and -(d+2). For d even the unique r=d/2 merges three modes into a signed triangle with eigenvalues (d-2,d-2,-(2d+2)); remaining modes sit at -2 or axis level d-2. Multiplicity sums equal 3d² and top eigenvalue 4d-2 is simple, proving connectedness. Kirchhoff gives the exact stated spanning-tree product; the old Gram-rank formula follows from shifting adjacency by 2-d. Independent exact graph construction and adjacency diagonalization for d=3,4,5,6 matched each predicted eigenvalue/multiplicity. Finite experiments only corroborate the all-d Fourier proof.
